title_fa: آغاز به کار تاکسی‌های بدون فرمان و پدال تسلا در تگزاس
title_en: تسلا سفر با تاکسی‌های خودران Cybercab را در تگزاس آغاز کرد [تماشا کنید]تسلا سفر با تاکسی‌های خودران ...
summary: تسلا ارائه خدمات سرویس تاکسی روباتیک دونفره سایبرکپ (Cybercab) را بدون فرمان و پدال در بخش‌هایی از شهر آستین آغاز کرد.
سایبرکپ نخستین خودروی تسلا محسوب می‌شود که به‌طور اختصاصی برای رانندگی خودکار بدون نیاز به ناظر انسانی طراحی شده است.
مقررات فعلی فدرال آمریکا فروش گسترده خودروهای بدون کنترل دستی را محدود کرده و نهادهای ایمنی در حال بررسی فعالیت جدید تسلا هستند.
با وجود حضور ۴۵ دستگاه سایبرکپ تسلا در تگزاس، رقیب اصلی آن یعنی وایمو نزدیک به ۱۰۰۰ خودروی فعال در این ایالت دارد.
full_text: تسلا ارائه سفر با تاکسی خودران دونفره Cybercab را در مناطق محدودی از آستین تگزاس آغاز کرد. این خودرو برخلاف خودروهای معمولی فاقد فرمان و پدال است و اداره ملی ایمنی ترافیک بزرگراههای آمریکا (NHTSA) نیز اعلام کرده در حال بررسی این فعالیت تسلا است. تسلا اعلام کرده Cybercab درحالحاضر فقط در بخشهایی از آستین قابل استفاده است و هر فردی میتواند با آن سفر کند. مدیر بخش هوش مصنوعی تسلا در مراسم معرفی خودرو گفت: «این سرویس برای عموم مردم باز است.» تسلا هنوز زمان آغاز دریافت هزینه از مسافران را اعلام نکرده است. بااینحال، مدیران شرکت در مراسم گفتند قصد دارند از قیمتگذاری پویا استفاده کنند؛ به این معنا که هزینه سفر با افزایش تقاضا بیشتر خواهد شد. آنها همچنین وعده ارائه «تجربهای درجهیک با قیمت کلاس اقتصادی» را مطرح کردند. Cybercab بدون فرمان و پدال به گفته رویترز، Cybercab اولین خودروی تسلا است که برای استفاده کاملاً خودران و بدون نظارت انسانی طراحی شده است. «ایلان ماسک» در ویدیویی جدید آن را «اولین خودرویی که بهطور خاص برای رانندگی کاملاً خودران و بدون نظارت ساخته شده» توصیف کرد. تسلا در هفتههای اخیر مراسم رونمایی Cybercab را در آستین تبلیغ کرده بود. برخی سرمایهگذاران و چهرههای فعال در شبکههای اجتماعی برای شرکت در این رویداد به تگزاس رفتند و ویدیوهایی از سفر خود با خودرو منتشر کردند. تسلا درحالحاضر سرویس محدودی از تاکسیهای خودران را با ناوگانی از خودروهای Model Y ارائه میکند که برخی از آنها ناظر ایمنی انسانی دارند. این شرکت قصد دارد در ادامه Cybercab بدون فرمان را به مدل اصلی خودروهای بدون راننده در شبکه بزرگتر تاکسیهای خودرانش تبدیل کند. قوانین ایمنی فدرال آمریکا معمولاً وجود کنترلهای دستی برای خودروها را الزامی میکند. مقررات فعلی همچنین تعداد خودروهایی را که هر تولیدکننده میتواند بدون فرمان و پدال به فروش برساند، محدود کرده است. بااینحال، خودروسازان باسابقه میتوانند تعداد نامحدودی از چنین خودروهایی را برای آزمایش به کار بگیرند. مشخص نیست تسلا با چه سرعتی میتواند Cybercab را در مقیاس گسترده به کار بگیرد. در کالیفرنیا، که از بازارهای مهم آمریکا محسوب میشود، تسلا مجوز فعالیت بهعنوان تاکسی خودران یا آزمایش خودروهای بدون راننده را بدون حضور راننده ایمنی در صندلی جلو ندارد. بر اساس سوابق ایالت تگزاس، تسلا تا عصر چهارشنبه ۴۲۰ خودروی خودران در این ایالت ثبت کرده بود که ۴۵ دستگاه از آنها Cybercab هستند. تعداد ثبتشده خودروهای تسلا در همین روز در مقطعی ۳۱۴ دستگاه اعلام شده بود. در مقابل، Waymo، رقیب اصلی تسلا در تاکسیهای بدون راننده در آمریکا، ۹۸۸ خودروی خودران در تگزاس ثبت کرده است. خودروهای Waymo برخلاف Cybercab همچنان دارای کنترلهای دستی هستند، اما در هنگام استفاده از حالت خودران راننده انسانی ندارند.
impact: گامی کلیدی اما پرچالش برای تجاری‌سازی تاکسی‌های تمام‌خودران تسلا و ورود به رقابت جدی با وایمو.

title_fa: رونمایی آروان‌کلاد از AI Canvas؛ طراحی زیرساخت ابری با دستور متنی و صوتی
title_en: پرده آخر ترومن‌شوی آروان‌کلاد با رونمایی AI Canvas در الکامپ ۱۴۰۵
summary: آروان‌کلاد در نمایشگاه الکامپ از دستیار جدیدی رونمایی کرد که معماری کامل ابری را بر اساس نیاز کاربر به‌صورت گرافیکی می‌سازد.
این ابزار با پشتیبانی از پروتکل MCP، ارتباط میان سرویس‌های مختلف ابری را خودکار کرده و فرایند استقرار را سرعت می‌بخشد.
full_text: پرده آخر ترومنشوی آروانکلاد با رونمایی AI Canvas در الکامپ ۱۴۰۵ آروانکلاد در نمایشگاه الکامپ ۱۴۰۵ از AI Canvas، ابزار جدید خود برای طراحی و اجرای معماری زیرساخت ابری با کمک هوش مصنوعی، رونمایی کرد. آروانکلاد در نخستین روز از نمایشگاه الکامپ ۱۴۰۵ از AI Canvas، ابزار جدید خود برای طراحی و اجرای معماری زیرساخت ابری با کمک هوش مصنوعی، رونمایی کرد. این دستیار هوش مصنوعی با استفاده از تعامل متنی و صوتی، نیاز کاربر را از مرحلهی سفارش نوع کسبوکار دریافت میکند و با فراخواندن محصولات متنوع ابری، یک معماری ابری کاربردی و آماده برای راهاندازی محصول فراهم میکند. آروانکلاد در چهار روز از نمایشگاه الکامپ ۱۴۰۵ در سالن ۸ و ۹ میزبان بازدیدکنندگان و کسبوکارهای مختلف است و امروز دوازدهم شهریور میزبان بازدیدکنندگان است. بازدیدکنندگان در این غرفه با جدیدترین راهکارها و محصولات آروان آشنا شده و از نزدیک میتوانند پرسشها و دغدغههای خود را با متخصصان آروانی مطرح کنند. در غرفهی آروانکلاد متخصصان آروانی از تیمهای مختلف حضور دارند تا به بهترین شکل کاربران و بازدیدکنندگان را راهنمایی کنند و آخرین تجربههایشان را به اشتراک بگذارند. AI Canvas؛ تونلی در دل هوش مصنوعی تونل «بوم هوش مصنوعی» یکی از بخشهای اصلی غرفه آروان است که در آن AI Canvas روی ویدیووالها به بازدیدکنندگان معرفی میشود. در این ابزار، کاربر میتواند نیاز خود را بهشکل متنی یا صوتی بیان کند یا یکی از سناریوهای آماده را انتخاب کند. AI Canvas براساس این ورودی، سرویسهای موردنیاز و ارتباط میان آنها را در قالب یک گراف معماری ایجاد میکند و پس از تایید کاربر، زیرساخت برای مرحله استقرار آماده میشود. در این بخش، بازدیدکنندگان با یک «بوم هوش مصنوعی آروان» روبهرو میشوند؛ فضایی تعاملی که در آن سرویسهای ابری از طریق یک گفتوگوی ساده به یکدیگر متصل شده و معماری موردنیاز شکل میگیرد. کاربر میتواند بدون درگیری با دانش زیرساخت ابری، نیاز خود را با این بوم هوش مصنوعی آروان مطرح کند و یا از میان سناریوهای آماده یکی را انتخاب کند. پس از آن، کارتهای سرویسها، ارتباط میان اجزا و ساختار معماری بهشکل خودکار روی صفحه ایجاد میشوند. گراف نهایی نیز امکان ذخیرهسازی و Import دارد و میتواند بهعنوان ورودی مرحله استقرار زیرساخت استفاده شود. در مرحله بعد، Agent آروان میتواند فرایند آمادهسازی و استقرار زیرساخت را انجام دهد و خطاهای شناساییشده در فرآیند را برطرف کند. هدف AI Canvas کوتاهکردن مسیر میان یک ایده اولیه تا طراحی و اجرای زیرساخت موردنیاز آن است. AI Canvas نخستین محصول آروان است که از MCP Server آروان برای تعامل مدلهای هوش مصنوعی با سرویسهای ابری استفاده میکند. در حال حاضر بیشتر سرویسهای آروان از طریق این MCP Server در دسترس هستند. مدیر محصول AIaaS آروان، آرش جهانگیری دربارهی این محصول جدید میگوید: «آروان کلاد همیشه به دنبال آن بوده تا زیرساختهای ابری را در یک فضای یکپارچه ارایه دهد. ترکیب هوش مصنوعی و MCP آروان باعث شده تا بوم هوش مصنوعی آروان به قدمی بزرگ در ارایهی زیرساخت یکپارچه ابری تبدیل شود. در واقع AI canvas ترندهایی مانند Cloud AI، Agentic Platform و No Code Low Code Deployment را دنبال میکند». پلی بین الکامپ و سینما بهطور کلی طراحی غرفه امسال برداشتی آزاد از فیلم The Truman Show بود، فیلمی که به آزادی، اراده و اختیار انسانها میپردازد و تلاش شده در طراحی غرفه علاوه بر جنبهی بصری به روایت بخشی از ارزشهای آروانکلاد پرداخته شود. میثم خاوری مدیر هنری آروانکلاد دربارهی ایدهی اولیه و چرایی این طراحی توضیح میدهد: «با توجه به ماهیت آروانکلاد و زیرساخت ابری، ابر و آسمان در طراحیهای بصری ما جزوی جداناشدنی هستند و در کمپین پیشین نیز پروانهای در آسمان طراحی شد. برای طراحی غرفه نیز به دنبال آسمانی بزرگ و پر ابر بودیم و به یاد سکانس آخر فیلم نمایش ترومن، تصمیم گرفتم آن را در این طراحی نیز بگنجانم. بنابراین غرفهی ما در عین سادگی و ارتباط با ابر، به این فیلم و قاب معروف آن ارجاع میدهد. ترومن در این فیلم مسیری را برای رسیدن به آگاهی و آزادی طی میکند بنابراین وجود یک Journey در طراحی تونل با AI Canvas پیوند خورد و این تجربهی تعاملی خلق شد». در دو ضلع غرفه درختهایی وجود دارند که استعارهای از دو مسوولیت اجتماعی آروان، کاریز و آروان آکادمی هستند. در گوشهای دیگر از غرفه پروانهای به عنوان نماد تولدی دوباره برای راهکارهای بازیابی پس از حادثه طراحی شده که بر اهمیت پیشبینی و معماری مناسب برای روزهای حادثه تاکید میکند. خود غرفه از دو طبقه سازه تشکیل شده که طبقه بالا اتاقهای جلسه برای دیدار و گفتوگو با مخاطبان و کسبوکارها تدارک دیده شده و طبقه همکف زیر اتاق جلسات، تونل بزرگی وجود دارد که تجربهای تعاملی از نحوه طراحی زیرساخت ابری را به نمایش میگذارد. طبقات بالا با پلههایی سرخابی رنگ به همکف وصل میشود که یادآور قاب معروف ترومن شو است. بازدیدکنندگان با حضور در غرفه، گرفتن عکس و تگ کردن آروان در شبکههای اجتماعی میتوانند تا پنجاه میلیون تومان کد هدیه استفاده از همهی محصولات آروان را دریافت کنند. بازیابی پس از بحران و پروانهها یکی دیگر از محورهای اصلی حضور آروانکلاد در الکامپ، اتصال دو حوزهی Cloud و AI است؛ ترکیبی که به یکی از روندهای مهم توسعهی زیرساختهای فناوری در جهان تبدیل شده است. سرویس هوش مصنوعی آروانکلاد با هدف کمک به کسبوکارها برای آموزش مدلهای زبانی، توسعه و استقرار اپلیکیشنهای مبتنی بر هوش مصنوعی ارایه شده است. در این بخش، ابزارهایی مانند پایگاه دانش RAG و Guardrail قرار دارند که با هدف سادهسازی استفاده از دادهها و دانش سازمانی در راهکارهای هوش مصنوعی توسعه یافتهاند. در کنار هوش مصنوعی، یکی از مهمترین موضوعات مطرحشده در غرفهی آروانکلاد، مسالهی Disaster Recovery یا بازیابی پس از بحران است؛ موضوعی که با افزایش وابستگی کسبوکارها به زیرساختهای دیجیتال، اهمیت بیشتری پیدا کرده است. آروانکلاد در الکامپ امسال تلاش کرده مجموعهای از این رویکردها را در کنار یکدیگر ارایه دهد؛ از توسعهی محصولات ابری و ابزارهای هوش مصنوعی گرفته تا راهکارهای مرتبط با تابآوری و بازیابی پس از بحران. طراحی متفاوت غرفه نیز با هدف ایجاد یک تجربهی تعاملی برای بازدیدکنندگان انجام شده تا مخاطبان تنها با فهرستی از محصولات مواجه نباشند، بلکه بخشی از فرآیند طراحی و استفاده از زیرساختهای ابری را نیز تجربه کنند. غرفهی آروانکلاد در سالن ۸ و ۹ نمایشگاه بینالمللی الکامپ قرار دارد و بازدیدکنندگان میتوانند تا ۱۲ شهریورماه از این فضا و راهکارهای ابری و هوش مصنوعی این شرکت بازدید کنند.
impact: تسهیل و تسریع فرایند راه‌اندازی زیرساخت‌های ابری برای تیم‌های فنی و استارتاپ‌ها.

Conclusion Cerebras Systems sits in that dangerous sweet spot Tim Sykes talks about all the time: massive story, massive volatility. full_text: The United States’ top automotive safety regulator has opened an investigation into Tesla’s decision to launch its new Cybercab on public roads with no steering wheel or pedals. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) announced Friday morning that it opened the probe mere hours after Tesla put the first Cybercabs on the streets of Austin, Texas. Federal vehicle safety regulations require manual controls like brake pedals, though the Department of Transportation recently proposed removing those requirements for vehicles that are designed to be autonomously driven. “NHTSA fully supports the safe development and deployment of automated vehicles. But as the federal regulator, we need to ensure that all of our laws are followed,” administrator Jonathan Morrison said in a statement. “Our approach of balancing innovation with safety oversight will allow the United States to maintain its global leadership in AV innovation.” NHTSA said Friday that Tesla told the agency it self-certified the Cybercab as being compliant with all of the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS). Automakers traditionally self-certify whether their vehicles comply with FMVSS rules. In the filing, the agency said it was opening the investigation to “examine the process and technical data on which Tesla relied when certifying the Cybercab and related issues.” NHTSA said it will consider the extent to which the company’s certification depended on determinations that certain federal motor standards are inapplicable to the Cybercab. There is precedent to NHTSA’s inquiry. In 2022, Amazon-owned autonomous vehicle company Zoox self-certified its cube-like robotaxi, which lacks traditional controls such as a steering wheel and pedals. NHTSA then opened up what it called a “special order” seeking more information from Zoox and formally launched an audit query — the same process it is now using for Tesla — the following the year. While Zoox was still heavily in its testing phase at that time, the investigation did slow its path to commercialization. Zoox had long maintained that the self-certification process was sufficient and in 2025 the federal agency gave the company an exemption to demonstrate — not commercially operate — its technology. Zoox then went through the official process and filed for a temporary Part 555 exemption from eight Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards in hopes it would get the final OK that would allow it to charge for robotaxi rides. Zoox received final approval for that exemption in July 2026, eliminating one of the last remaining regulatory hurdles the company needed to clear before launching a commercial robotaxi service. The exemption did place some limits on Zoox. Under the temporary exemption, Zoox can add 2,500 vehicles per year to its commercial fleet over the next for two years. Zoox opened its commercial service several weeks later and now charges for rides in Las Vegas. Whether Tesla will face a similarly long process is unclear. Zoox navigated the regulatory process under the Biden and Trump administrations. On Friday, NHTSA acknowledged that it is in the process of changing some parts of the FMVSS that relate to manual controls in order to “unleash American innovation and enhance safety on our roads.” The agency said it “looks forward to finishing these critical updates and removing unnecessary barriers to American AV innovation in the coming months. Until that work is completed, however, existing standards remain in force.” This story has been updated with new information from NHTSA.

full_text: Startup funding this week (August 31-September 4, 2026) highlighted a broad appetite for companies building infrastructure around artificial intelligence, healthcare, semiconductors, and clean energy. From a $165 million Series C for robotics perception startup Lyte to fresh capital for Indian deep-tech ventures, investors backed businesses targeting some of the technology sector’s biggest challenges. US-based Lyte raised $165 million in a Series C round led by Maverick Silicon, valuing the robotics perception company at $1.6 billion. Lyte develops custom silicon, multimodal sensors and spatial software that help robots interpret their surroundings. The company said the new capital will support production, AI and perception development, and wider deployments across robotics and industrial customers. Healthcare technology company PatientIQ also secured $30 million in Series C funding, led by Hughes & Company. The Chicago-based company provides an outcomes intelligence platform used by more than 870 healthcare organizations and 17 million patients in the US. PatientIQ plans to expand into additional medical specialties, strengthen its real-world evidence platform and develop its direct-to-patient marketplace. Creator marketing platform Archive closed a strategic funding round backed by Anti Fund and Florida Funders, with participation from Battery Ventures, Stripe, Tiger Global, Lux Capital, Human Capital, and more than 50 founders and technology and consumer executives. The company did not disclose the size of the round. Archive uses AI-powered technology to help brands monitor social content and manage creator campaigns, from identifying influencers to turning successful posts into paid advertising. More than 1,000 brands currently use the platform, while two major AI labs are also running creator marketing campaigns through Archive. India’s deep-tech ecosystem also featured prominently. Zenergize Technologies raised $4 million in a Pre-Series A round led by Giraffe Studios, combining equity and venture debt. The company develops Silicon Carbide-based power electronics for applications including solar inverters and EV charging. The funding will support manufacturing expansion, engineering, R&D, and its sales and service network. Also Read: Piyush Goyal Proposes India-Japan Shark Tank Series to Boost Startup Funding Semiconductor metrology startup Makr Microsystems raised Rs. 10.2 crore in seed funding led by Bluehill VC, with Artha Venture Fund participating. Makr is developing Acoustic Atomic Force Microscopy, a technology designed to inspect structures beneath semiconductor surfaces without damaging them. The startup plans to use the capital for technology development, customer validation, and commercial deployment. Together, the week’s funding activity points to continued investor interest in specialized technology. Robotics perception, healthcare data, creator marketing, power electronics, and semiconductor inspection may serve different markets, but each targets infrastructure gaps that could become increasingly important as AI and advanced manufacturing expand.

full_text: Microsoft is giving its developer-optimized Windows experience a name: Project Zenith. While the software maker originally announced a similar developer-optimized Windows effort at Build earlier this year, Project Zenith is designed for new developer-focused devices with 64GB or more of unified memory. Microsoft’s Project Zenith is a ‘distraction-free Windows experience’ for developers The first Project Zenith devices ship with AMD’s Ryzen AI Halo chips. The first Project Zenith devices ship with AMD’s Ryzen AI Halo chips. “Project Zenith devices come with a preconfigured Windows setup for development and a set of tools curated for what developers reach for first,” explains Logan Iyer, CVP of Windows platform and developer at Microsoft. “On these devices, developers can run 30B+ parameter models locally and unmetered — accelerating experimentation while helping reduce reliance on metered cloud tokens.” AMD announced the first Project Zenith device on stage at IFA earlier today, a miniature PC powered by Ryzen AI Halo chips. There will be more Project Zenith devices “in the coming months,” including ones with different silicon. These Project Zenith devices will include preinstalled developer tools like Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot, PowerToys, WinAppCLI, and Windows Dev Skills. The File Explorer has also been configured to show file extensions, hidden files, and the full path in the title bar. Microsoft has also disabled recently used files and folders and sync provider tips, as well as enabling long-path support. Start menu tips and account notifications are also turned off, and the PowerToys Command Palette is enabled by default. Some of these changes feel like ones that should just be enabled by default on every Windows 11 install, particularly anything that removes the annoying distractions in the operating system. Microsoft has been on a mission this year to greatly improve Windows 11, and Project Zenith is the developer-side effort. “Project Zenith is the result of listening to developers about what they need from Windows today, and where they want the platform to go next,” says Iyer. “As AI continues to transform software development, we are committed to evolving Windows alongside the community that builds on it.”
impact: تحول در تجربه برنامه‌نویسی محلی و کاهش وابستگی استارتاپ‌ها به APIهای گران‌قیمت ابری.

full_text: Ugreen, known for its phone power banks, chargers, and NAS storage solutions, is moving into the smart home — in a big way. This week at the IFA tech show, the company launched its HomeAgent smart home platform that combines security camera storage, on-device AI, and smart home control in one system, managed by a voice assistant called Uliya, with the promise that everything runs locally. This NAS company wants to run your local smart home Ugreen’s HomeAgent combines a NAS, a security camera NVR, and an on-device AI assistant in one box, maxing out with a $9,999 Nvidia Jetson Thor version. Ugreen’s HomeAgent combines a NAS, a security camera NVR, and an on-device AI assistant in one box, maxing out with a $9,999 Nvidia Jetson Thor version. At the core of Ugreen’s HomeAgent system is a hub that acts as the brain of your smart home, running a local-first AI (with some caveats) that you can interact with using natural language via Uliya. There are three hub configurations to choose from, each of which stores all data locally and processes video footage on-device, keeping it local and private and without monthly subscription fees. Albeit likely at a higher upfront cost. The big pitch is that your data never needs to leave your home, addressing two key smart-home concerns: privacy and recurring subscriptions. Ugreen says its powerful AI runs on the hub, providing features like cross-camera tracking, smart alerts for people, vehicles, pets, and packages, and live status questions such as “where is my pet now?” There’s also AI-powered video search and text descriptions of events, along with natural language voice control of smart home devices and automations. Along with local storage of your camera footage, the system can store personal files, including music, movies, and photos, just like a NAS. All this comes without monthly storage fees for video footage that are common with popular cloud-based solutions, such as Amazon’s Ring and Alexa and Google’s Nest cameras and Gemini for Home. The HomeAgent HA100 will launch with early bird pricing of $899 which increases to $2999 of the HA100 Pro, and a whopping $9999 for the Nvidia-powered MasterAgent MA100 model. The systems will launch on Kickstarter in October, after which Ugreen suggests that pricing will roughly double. The idea of combining your digital home and life on a single hub that uses local AI to store, manage, and run everything is fast gaining traction. Companies like SwitchBot, Reolink, and Aqara have made moves in this space, and this week at IFA, Anker launched a similar product called the Eufy MindBase. Both systems use the Matter smart home standard to incorporate smart home devices from different brands. I visited Ugreen’s booth at IFA and got a hands-on demo, where I controlled Nanoleaf lights alongside smart blinds with voice commands to Uliya via the HomeAgent hub. The HomeAgent hub is a Matter controller and will support third-party devices using Wi-Fi, Zigbee, Thread, Bluetooth, NFC, ONVIF/RTSP, and PoE. Ugreen says it will publish a device compatibility list, which is currently fairly small and includes devices from Aqara, ThirdReality, SwitchBot, and Eve. In theory, any Matter device should work, but the first phase supports only lights, switches, sensors, and curtains — and the company advises sticking with products it has approved. Ugreen is also launching a smart speaker to run Uliya, along with a line of security cameras: the SynCare Indoor Cam ID500 Pro, the SynCare POE Cam OD600 Pro, and a battery-powered SynCare Cam OD800 Pro. A unique integration is with Ugreen’s new E Ink Spectra-powered digital photo frame that can display your photos stored on the hub, which again need never go into the cloud. The three versions of the HomeAgent hub offer increasing levels of compute for more advanced processing and broader AI-powered features: The HomeAgent HA100 can execute simple, basic rule-based automation and control using specific voice commands; the HomeAgent HA100 Pro adds semantic and context-aware understanding; and the MasterAgent MA100 version brings the highest level of local compute power via an NVIDIA Jetson Thor T5000 platform. While everything can run locally on the HomeAgent, features such as push notifications and remote viewing of your security camera footage require internet access. There is also an option to use the cloud for the Uliya voice assistant. Keeping all your data inside your home, while still enjoying the benefits AI can bring to managing your smart home and digital life, is a compelling idea. Whether Ugreen’s Home Agent succeeds will depend on how well it integrates with what you already own and how easy it is to set up and use. Photos by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

title_en: NVIDIA (NVDA)’s Hugging Face Deal Tests the Next Phase of its AI Strategy
summary: انویدیا با تصاحب ۱۲.۹ میلیارد دلاری هاگینگ‌فیس، جایگاه خود را در زیست‌بوم هوش مصنوعی متن‌باز فوق‌العاده تقویت کرد.

full_text: NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) has agreed to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.93 billion, making it one of Nvidia's largest acquisitions. The deal gives Nvidia a much stronger position in open-source/open-weight AI, an area gaining traction because developers can customize models and potentially deploy them at lower costs than proprietary alternatives. Hugging Face has more than 18 million users and millions of models, datasets, and applications, giving NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) access to a large developer community. Nvidia says the platform will remain open and continue supporting models and hardware from different vendors. The acquisition also fits Nvidia's broader strategy of expanding beyond GPUs and becoming a more influential player across the AI ecosystem. The company has increasingly used investments and partnerships with AI companies to reinforce demand for its computing infrastructure. An Expanding AI Opportunity The acquisition could help NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) move beyond supplying the chips used to train and run AI models. Hugging Face gives Nvidia exposure to the developer and model layer, allowing it to participate more directly in how AI models are created, distributed, and deployed. That could strengthen Nvidia's strategic position as AI adoption expands. A larger open-model ecosystem could ultimately benefit Nvidia's core semiconductor business. Developers building, fine-tuning and deploying models require significant computing resources, and Nvidia could use its relationship with Hugging Face's large developer base to encourage more workloads on Nvidia-powered infrastructure. Reuters notes that the deal is intended partly to strengthen Nvidia's connections with developers and potentially increase demand for its processors. NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) is not betting exclusively on proprietary AI models from companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. By owning Hugging Face, it gains exposure if open-weight models become an increasingly important part of the AI market. Barron's characterized the transaction as giving Nvidia exposure to the rapidly expanding open-model segment while positioning it alongside proprietary AI. Owning Hugging Face could prevent another major technology company from acquiring a platform that has become important to the AI developer ecosystem. It also gives Nvidia a stronger position against growing competition, including open-weight AI models emerging from China. Risks Behind the Expansion At nearly $13 billion, the acquisition is a significant investment for a platform that was valued at $4.5 billion in its last reported funding round in 2023. NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) will need to generate meaningful strategic and financial value from Hugging Face to justify the substantial premium. Hugging Face's appeal comes partly from its open nature. Nvidia's ownership could raise concerns that the platform may eventually favor Nvidia hardware or models. Reuters reported that some analysts and developers worry Nvidia could prioritize its own hardware at the expense of competing chip providers. Even if Nvidia maintains its current commitment to openness, perceptions of reduced neutrality could undermine Hugging Face's appeal.

full_text: Get tech news that matters delivered weekly. Join 50,000+ readers. Google has unveiled WeatherNext 3, a global weather AI model that generates a new forecast every hour at up to 5-kilometer resolution, a step up from the six-hour data lag typical of models trainedon numerical weather prediction simulations. According to Google, the model draws on a continuously updating feed of geostationary satellite imagery worldwide and learns directly from scattered ground station readings, letting it reflect local features such as terrain. This approach aims to address rapid weather changes and local variations in temperature and humidity that traditional models miss. Google says the model is particularly beneficial for regions in Latin America, Africa, and Asia-Pacific that have historically lacked high-resolution forecasting due to the high supercomputing costs of traditional regional models. WeatherNext 3 also adds predictions aimed at renewable energy production, covering wind speeds 100 meters up, near turbine height, plus detailed cloud cover and incoming solar radiation. Google says that data should help grid operators and renewable energy developers line up expected output from wind and solar assets with demand. For precipitation, the model is trained on NASA's satellite-based IMERG data and Google's own global precipitation reanalysis. In medium-range forecasts, Google reports a Continuous Ranked Probability Score improvement of up to 60% against IMERG, 30% against MRMS, and 10% against rain gauge measurements for early lead times. The announcement follows Google's broader push into AI infrastructure, including its Project Suncatcher orbital data center initiative, which aims to network solar-powered satellitesequipped with Tensor Processing Units. Nvidia’s N1X laptop will ship in two different configurations for laptops and mini PCs. You’ll be able to buy an RTX Spark N1X laptop with a configuration that I would call the mini PC chip. The top of the line N1X chip comes with a 6144-core Blackwell RTX GPU, paired with a 20-core Grace CPU and between 24GB and 128GB of unified memory. This particular chip will ship in both high-end laptops and miniature PCs like Microsoft’s Surface RTX Spark Dev Box. The more cut down N1X, or what I’d call the laptop chip, has a 5120-core Blackwell RTX GPU, combined with an 18-core Grace CPU and between 24GB and 32GB of unified memory. I’d expect most RTX Spark N1x laptops are going to use this chip, with devices launching from Asus, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft, or MSI in October. We’re still waiting for Nvidia to share more on what the N1X is capable of for laptop gaming, but the company is vaguely promising 100fps 1440p gaming with ray-tracing and DLSS enabled for now. RTX Spark laptops are only a month away, so we’re also waiting to hear about exact availability and pricing from PC makers. With a RAMageddon crisis still looming large, I’m expecting to see N1X laptops priced at the very premium end of the market.

The new investment will primarily support the development of additional products. It also seeks to strengthen its position in the local gaming market. The strategy allows Takahouse to apply what it has learned from WhistGame across a broader product portfolio. It also creates a path to reduce reliance on a single title as the company works to establish itself as a developer and publisher. The Ripple Takahouse’s funding adds to the flow of investment into Saudi Arabia’s gaming sector, where local companies are seeking to develop products for both regional and international audiences. For the startup, expanding from one established title into multiple products will test whether its social gaming approach can translate across different concepts and audiences. It will also place greater demands on development resources as Takahouse moves from building an individual game toward a broader publishing model. What to Watch The key signal will be how Takahouse deploys the USD 1.5 million into its product pipeline. title_fa: احتمال تصاحب ۷ میلیارد دلاری استارتاپ Decart توسط آنتروپیک
title_en: The 48 hours that rewrote Israel's startup rankings
summary: ارزش‌گذاری استارتاپ‌های فناوری در اسرائیل طی ماه‌های اخیر جهش‌های چند میلیارد دلاری تجربه کرده است.
آنتروپیک در حال مذاکره پیشرفته برای خرید ۷ میلیارد دلاری استارتاپ زیرساختی Decart است.
این قرارداد در صورت نهایی شدن، بزرگ‌ترین خرید تاریخ آنتروپیک محسوب خواهد شد.
full_text: The 48 hours that rewrote Israel's startup rankings Wonderful, Upwind and HiBob all revealed sharply higher price tags this week, and one rising star may already be on its way out the door. In the span of about 48 hours this week, three Israeli technology companies added a combined $5.7 billion to their paper valuations. Wonderful, an AI customer-service startup, was valued at $5 billion after a $550 million raise, its third fundraising round in under a year and a jump from $2 billion just six months earlier. Upwind, a cloud-security firm, more than doubled its own valuation to $3.8 billion in five months. And HiBob, a human-resources software maker, was valued at $3.5 billion after Salesforce led a $166 million investment. None of the three companies had done anything as dramatic as ship a breakthrough product or land a marquee customer in the days before their new price tags were set. What changed, mostly, was investors' willingness to keep paying up, a pattern that has become the defining feature of Israeli tech funding since 2024, when the sector began climbing out of a slump brought on by a judicial overhaul fight and the war that followed October 7. The result, drawn from a full accounting of every disclosed Israeli funding round since the start of 2024, is a ranking of the country's 15 most valuable startups that would have been unrecognizable three years ago. It is also a ranking that may already be out of date: Decart, the AI infrastructure company sitting at number nine with a $4 billion valuation from a funding round in May, is in advanced talks to be acquired by Anthropic, the AI lab behind the Claude chatbot, in a deal that people close to the negotiations say could value the company at around $7 billion. If it closes, it would be Anthropic's largest acquisition to date, and would remove one of Israel's fastest-rising startups from the ranks of independent companies just months after it arrived there. A list built on the last two years, not the last decade Unlike most "most valuable startup" rankings, which tend to accumulate valuations set years or even a decade apart, this one is built entirely from rounds raised since January 2024. That makes it, in one sense, a narrower slice of the Israeli tech landscape, older companies that haven't needed to raise money recently, or that have simply stopped growing, don't appear. But it also makes the numbers unusually current: nearly every valuation on the list was set in the past two years, and several were set in the past two days. In an industry where a "unicorn" badge earned in 2021 can be a stale and even misleading signal today, that recency is arguably the more meaningful measure of where investor money is actually flowing right now. At the top of the list sits Vast Data, the data-infrastructure company that reached a $30 billion valuation in April after raising $1 billion amid the broader AI computing buildout. Vast Data's ascent to the top spot was itself a byproduct of another deal. The company became Israel's most valuable private tech firm only after Wiz, the cybersecurity startup that had held that title, was sold to Google. Deel, the global payroll company co-founded by an Israeli entrepreneur, ranks second at $17.3 billion after a $300 million round last October. Cyera, a data-security startup, is third at $12 billion, having quadrupled its valuation in eighteen months. Its CEO, Yotam Segev, has said the company's ambition is to become "the CrowdStrike of data security." Look past the top three and the list is dominated by cybersecurity companies, a reflection of Israel's long-standing strength in the field and of enterprise customers' bottomless appetite for tools to secure an increasingly AI-driven workplace. DriveNets, a networking company, ranks fourth at $8.5 billion after telling investors it is now cash-flow positive with more than $1 billion in order backlog. Cato Networks and Island, both cybersecurity firms, are tied at $4.8 billion; Island's valuation has more than quadrupled since October 2023 as demand grows for "enterprise browsers" that give companies more control over how employees interact with corporate data. Claroty, which protects industrial and infrastructure systems from cyberattacks, sits at $3 billion. Rapyd, a fintech company, registered a $4.5 billion valuation in a raise this year used partly to fund its $610 million acquisition of the payments firm PayU. Notably though, this is well down from the $10 billion valuation the company achieved in 2021. What connects Wonderful, Upwind, Decart and much of the rest of the upper list is a broader dynamic playing out across global venture capital: valuations for companies seen as central to the AI buildout, whether they sell AI products directly or the infrastructure underneath them, are rising faster and more frequently than in almost any other category of startup. Wonderful's valuation rose from $34 million to $5 billion in roughly a year. Upwind doubled in five months. Decart, an AI infrastructure company, went from an initial funding round to a reported $4 billion valuation before the acquisition talks with Anthropic began. That velocity cuts both ways. Rapid re-pricing rewards founders and early investors, but it also means today's valuation is a bet on a still-unproven trajectory, not a settled judgment, and it raises the stakes for what happens if growth slows or a larger buyer simply writes a check instead of continuing to fund the run. Decart's likely exit is a reminder that in the current market, the fastest way to leave this list is not to fail, but to succeed enough to get bought. The list (top 15, by latest disclosed valuation since January 2024): Vast Data — $30 billion Deel — $17.3 billion Cyera — $12 billion DriveNets — $8.5 billion Wonderful — $5 billion Cato Networks — $4.8 billion Island — $4.8 billion Rapyd — $4.5 billion Decart — $4 billion (in advanced talks to be acquired by Anthropic for a reported ~$7 billion) Eon — $4 billion

title_fa: جاماندن چت‌بات Grok؛ نبرد پرهزینه ماسک در بازار هوش مصنوعی
title_en: ایلان ماسک و رویای ترک‌خورده هوش مصنوعی / ثروتمندترین مرد جهان در در بزرگ‌ترین نبرد فناوری‌ عقب ...
summary: مدل Grok و استارتاپ xAI برخلاف ChatGPT و Claude هنوز نتوانسته‌اند در لیست اپلیکیشن‌های پردانلود یا بازار سازمانی جایگاه محکمی پیدا کنند.
ایلان ماسک با تزریق ۱۵.۸ میلیارد دلار سرمایه قصد دارد زیرساخت پردازشی غول‌پیکری برای جبران این فاصله بسازد.
موفقیت ماسک به یکپارچه‌سازی هوش مصنوعی با خودروهای تسلا و شبکه ماهواره‌ای استارلینک بستگی دارد.
full_text: به گزارش خبرآنلاین، شرکت هوش مصنوعی ماسک یعنی xAI در ماههای اخیر از رقبایی مانند OpenAI، Anthropic و گوگل عقب مانده است. یکی از نشانههای این عقبماندگی، میزان استقبال کاربران از محصولات هوش مصنوعی است. ChatGPT، Gemini و Claude در میان ۲۵ اپلیکیشن برتر اپاستور اپل قرار دارند، اما Grok در این فهرست هم دیده نمیشود. در بازار سازمانی نیز وضعیت چندان بهتر نیست. Grok هنوز در فهرست گزینههای اصلی بسیاری از شرکتهای بزرگ قرار نگرفته و در رقابت برای جذب مشتریان تجاری، پشت سر رقبایی مانند Claude و ChatGPT حرکت میکند. حتی خود ماسک نیز اخیراً پذیرفته که Grok از رقبا عقب افتاده است. او گفته بود که SpaceXAI در رقابت هوش مصنوعی «عقب مانده» و اضافه کرده بود: «من به باختن عادت ندارم.» با این حال، ماسک قصد عقبنشینی ندارد. SpaceX در سهماهه اخیر حدود ۱۵.۸ میلیارد دلار در پروژههای هوش مصنوعی سرمایهگذاری کرده و گفته این هزینهها تنها آغاز کار است. هدف او ساخت ظرفیت پردازشی عظیم برای آموزش و اجرای مدلهای هوش مصنوعی در مقیاسی است که بتواند با بزرگترین شرکتهای این حوزه رقابت کند. مشکل اینجاست که رقبای ماسک نیز دست روی دست نگذاشتهاند. شرکتهایی مانند مایکروسافت، گوگل، متا، آمازون و دیگر غولهای فناوری در حال صرف صدها میلیارد دلار برای ساخت مراکز داده و زیرساختهای مورد نیاز هوش مصنوعی هستند. در چنین بازاری، عقب ماندن از نظر تعداد کاربران یا مشتریان سازمانی میتواند به معنای نیاز به سرمایهگذاری بیشتر برای جبران فاصله باشد. از سوی دیگر، کسبوکارهای اصلی SpaceX همچنان وضعیت قدرتمندی دارند. موشکهای این شرکت و شبکه ماهوارهای استارلینک از مهمترین داراییهای آن هستند. اما به نوشته Yahoo Finance، سرمایهگذاری سنگین در هوش مصنوعی میتواند فشار زیادی به ترازنامه شرکت وارد کند بهخصوص اگر Grok نتواند به سرعت سهم بیشتری از بازار به دست آورد. با این حال بازار هوش مصنوعی با سرعت زیادی تغییر میکند و رتبه امروز شرکتها لزوماً جایگاه آنها در سالهای آینده را تعیین نمیکند. علاوه بر این، ماسک روی ترکیب هوش مصنوعی با دیگر کسبوکارهایش، از خودروهای تسلا گرفته تا رباتها و زیرساختهای فضایی، حساب ویژهای باز کرده است. بنابراین مسئله اصلی برای ماسک فقط ساخت یک چتبات بهتر نیست او باید ثابت کند میلیاردها دلار سرمایهگذاری در هوش مصنوعی میتواند در نهایت به یک کسبوکار بزرگ و پایدار تبدیل شود. ۵۸۵۸
impact: سرمایه‌گذاری سنگین در زیرساخت‌ها بدون جذب سریع مشتریان سازمانی، فشار مالی شدیدی به کسب‌وکارهای ماسک وارد خواهد کرد.

summary: اوبر با همکاری استارتاپ بریتانیایی Wayve، اولین سرویس تاکسی خودران پولی را در لندن فعال کرد.

full_text: Uber launched a robotaxi service in London, beating Waymo to become the first to offer paid trips in autonomous vehicles in the city. The vehicles use autonomous driving tech developed by Wayve, a UK-based startup, and will initially feature safety drivers behind the wheel. Uber beats Waymo as first to launch robotaxis in London The cars have no lidar and no geofence, but still will have human safety drivers for the initial launch. The cars have no lidar and no geofence, but still will have human safety drivers for the initial launch. The launch is a milestone for Uber, which has been plotting a UK launch with Wayve for several years. In beating Waymo to the punch, it allows Uber to set the standard for the robotaxi experience for thousands of Londoners. It’s also an early test of whether there’s appetite for driverless ridehailing beyond the US and China, where most of the world’s robotaxis are currently clustered. (There’s a smattering in the Middle East, too.) London-based Uber customers who want to try out these new robot-controlled cars can indicate their preference in the app’s settings. When booking a ride through UberX, Uber Comfort, or Uber Electric, riders may be paired with a Wayve-developed autonomous vehicle, but it’s not a guarantee. Wayve is using Ford Mustang Mach-Es for its fleet, followed by the Nissan Leaf in the future. Safety drivers will monitor the driving from the front seat, though Uber says they won’t control the driving and will gradually be phased out in favor of fully driverless vehicles. Safety drivers are licensed by Transport for London (TfL), the city’s transit authority. Wayve has around 15 vehicles registered with TfL, so it may be difficult to get matched with one, at least initially. Uber says there will be no geofence — the virtual boundary within which robotaxis are programed to operate — because Wayve’s AV2.0 system is designed to move “beyond the constraints of traditional AV systems.” Wayve expects to offer service “across the entirety of London” not including the airports, Wayve spokesperson Julianne McGoldrick said in an email. On its website, Wayve describes its AV2.0 system: The traditional AV1.0 approach relies on hand-engineered stacks, HD maps and a rule-based approach – this limits scalability and the ability to rapidly generalize to new environments or complex scenarios. Wayve’s AV2.0 takes a different path – a single, learned AI driver trained to understand the world, anticipate risk, and adapt to new environments. The robotaxis will be maintained and serviced by Uber in partnership with UK fleet operator Otto Car. Wayve will stay in charge of the autonomous driving system. Wayve, which was founded in 2017 by a pair of machine learning PhD students from the University of Cambridge, says its autonomous driving system can learn on the go, adapting to new roads, weather, or driving scenarios much like a human driver. The vehicles use cameras and radar as part of their perception system — but notably do not use lidar, the laser sensor that Waymo and many other robotaxi operators rely on. This puts Wayve in a similar camp as Tesla, which also doesn’t use lidar for its robotaxis. Still, Wayve claims its system is hardware agnostic, thanks to a software stack that can run on whatever sensors and chips an automaker uses for its vehicles. While additional sensors like lidar can theoretically be integrated if a car manufacturer prefers them, Wayve’s AV2.0 is built to operate autonomously without HD maps or expensive sensors, the company says. In addition to Uber, Wayve is also working with Stellantis on hands-free driving tech. And earlier this year, the startup raised $1.2 billion from Uber, Nvidia, and Stellantis, as well as Nissan and Mercedes-Benz, according to TechCrunch. Waymo has said it will launch its robotaxis in London before the end of the year. In addition, Lyft is working with China’s Baidu on its own robotaxi service in the city, starting with the neighborhood of Brent. Uber has been lobbying for a hybrid network made up of human drivers and robotaxis, which clashes with Waymo’s vision of a driver-free, rider-only system. Waymo and Uber still work together in several cities, including Austin and Atlanta, but the companies have increasingly found themselves on opposite sides of the debate — prompting rumors of an imminent breakup. Meanwhile, Uber has made a big to-do about linking up with a variety of AV partners, including Zoox, Avride, Nuro, Motional, Waabi, and of course, Wayve. The company has said it plans on spending upwards of $10 billion to build out its robotaxi business over time. Update September 3rd: Updated to include additional details about Wayve’s fleet size and service area.

full_text: The Builders Stage is returning to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, bringing together founders, startup operators, and investors for practical conversations on what it takes to build and scale successful companies. Hear from startup and venture leaders shaping the tech ecosystem, including Grant Lee, CEO and co-founder of Gamma; Leah Solivan, founder and general partner at Precedent.vc; Robby Stein, VP of Product at Google; and more. Through candid conversations and real-world case studies, speakers will share actionable insights on fundraising, hiring, go-to-market strategy, AI, and the operational decisions that fuel startup growth. Join more than 10,000 founders, investors, startup operators, and technology leaders at Moscone Center in San Francisco on October 13-15. Register today and save before our next ticket price increase. Built for founders who are ready to scale Building a startup is one thing. Building a company that can scale is another challenge entirely. The Builders Stage is one of six industry-focused stages at Disrupt 2026, dedicated to helping founders navigate the challenges of growth, from raising capital and hiring top talent to building go-to-market engines and preparing for the jump from seed to Series A. Every session delivers practical strategies you can put to work immediately, plus opportunities to engage directly with speakers during live Q&A. Secure your pass to Disrupt 2026 today and save up to $330 before rates increase. Without further ado, here's your first look at the Builders Stage agenda, with more speakers and sessions to be announced as we get closer to the event. Builders Stage agenda How to Win When You're Not Building AI With Shan Shan, Investment Manager, Baillie Gifford; and Yuri Sagalov, Managing Director at General Catalyst AI may dominate the world of venture, but many enduring companies won't be those that sell AI models or agents. This session is for founders competing for attention in an AI-obsessed market. Panelists break down what actually matters now: efficient growth, retention, revenue quality, and disciplined execution, and why fundamentals, not hype, still build breakout businesses. What Happens When OpenAI Ships Your Roadmap With Michel Tricot, CEO and Co-founder, Airbyte; Rob Toews, Partner, Radical Ventures; and Linda Tong, CEO, Webflow Nearly all AI founders have the same worry these days: What if OpenAI or Anthropic launches a product that competes with mine? Even strong products are at risk of becoming features of the larger players. This session explores where defensibility exists and what founders can do if they do face competition from rapidly evolving AI giants.

title_fa: «بازار پیشرفته» طلاین؛ امکان سفارش‌گذاری قیمتی در معاملات آنلاین طلا
title_en: رئیس هیئت مدیره طلاین در گفتگو با دیجیاتو مطرح کرد: حرکت از خریدوفروش ساده به سمت توسعه ابزارهای ...
summary: پلتفرم طلاین با معرفی قابلیت «بازار پیشرفته» به کاربران اجازه می‌دهد قیمت پیشنهادی خرید و فروش خود را ثبت کنند.
این ابزار معامله‌گران فعال بازار را هدف گرفته که نگاه کوتاه مدت دارند و به دنبال معامله در نرخ خاصی هستند.
موانع حقوقی و رگولاتوری پیاده‌سازی این قابلیت پس از رایزنی‌های فنی و قانونی برطرف شده است.
full_text: پلتفرمهای آنلاین طلا در سالهای گذشته عمدتاً تجربهای ساده از خرید و فروش این دارایی را در اختیار کاربران قرار دادهاند. اما مصطفی افزونی، رئیس هیئتمدیره طلاین، به دیجیاتو میگوید بخشی از مسیر توسعه این پلتفرم حالا به سمت پاسخ به نیاز کاربرانی میرود که ابزارهای بیشتری برای انجام معاملات خود میخواهند. «بازار پیشرفته» یکی از نخستین محصولات این مسیر است؛ بازاری که در آن کاربران میتوانند سفارش خرید یا فروش خود را با قیمت مدنظرشان ثبت کنند تا در صورت مچ شدن سفارشها، معامله انجام شود. طلاین یکی از غرفههای پربازدید نمایشگاه الکامپ است که با مخاطبین خود ارتباط برقرار کرده و به معرفی خدماتش پرداخته است. با رئیس هیئت مدیره طلاین در این باره گفتگو کردیم که میتوانید در ادامه مشاهده کنید. چرا طلاین به سراغ بازار پیشرفته رفت؟ مدل رایج خریدوفروش در بسیاری از پلتفرمهای آنلاین طلا ساده است؛ کاربر با قیمت لحظهای اعلامشده، میزان مشخصی طلا میخرد یا دارایی خود را میفروشد. اما افزونی معتقد است بخشی از کاربران نیاز متفاوتی دارند. به گفته رئیس هیئتمدیره طلاین، این گروه از کاربران نگاه صرفاً بلندمدت و نگهداری طلا ندارند و فعالتر از دیگر کاربران بازار را دنبال میکنند. به همین دلیل، برای آنها اهمیت دارد که خرید یا فروش در قیمت مشخصی انجام شود. او درباره نیاز شکلگیری این محصول توضیح داد: «یک سری از کاربران هستند که میخواهند در قیمت خاصی طلا بخرند یا بفروشند و نگاه سرمایهگذاری به آن ندارند که بخواهند برای بلندمدت نگه دارند.» بازار پیشرفته طلاین برای پاسخ به همین نیاز طراحی شده است. در این مدل، کاربر میتواند سفارش خرید یا فروش خود را در قیمت مدنظر ثبت کند و با رسیدن قیمت به آن سطح، معامله انجام شود. افزونی درباره پیچیدگیهای فنی این موضوع به دیجیاتو میگوید: «توسعه این قابلیت با پیچیدگیهای فنی همراه بوده و در مقطعی نیز درباره وضعیت آن در فرآیندهای رگولاتوری ابهامهایی وجود داشته است که پس از پیگیریهای حقوقی و فنی، این مساله برطرف شده است.» آنها همچنین قرار است ابزارهای بیشتری برای معاملهگران حرفهای توسعه دهند. استقبال از پلتفرمهای طلا؛ با وجود تردیدها بخش دیگری از گفتگو با افزونی به استقبال بازدیدکنندگان از غرفههای پلتفرمهای طلا در الکامپ اختصاص داشت. او معتقد است این استقبال نشان میدهد اعتماد، همچنان یکی از مهمترین عوامل در تصمیم کاربران برای استفاده از خدمات پلتفرمهای آنلاین طلاست. افزونی با اشاره به فضایی که به گفته او پیش از نمایشگاه علیه پلتفرمهای طلا شکل گرفته بود، میگوید استقبال مردم از غرفهها نشان داد بخشی از کاربران همچنان به این کسبوکارها اعتماد دارند و مایلاند از نزدیک درباره نحوه فعالیت آنها اطلاعات بیشتری کسب کنند. به گفته او، بازدیدکنندگان غرفه طلاین نیز دو گروه هستند؛ گروهی که از قبل کاربر این پلتفرم بودند و گروهی که با وجود شناخت پلتفرمهای آنلاین طلا، هنوز برای استفاده از آنها به سطح کافی از اعتماد نرسیده بودند. او میگوید در گفتوگو با گروه دوم، فرایند فعالیت پلتفرم، دادهها و مجوزهای مرتبط برای بازدیدکنندگان توضیح داده شده است. رقابت بیشتر، خدمات متنوعتر رئیس هیئتمدیره طلاین در بخش دیگری از گفتگو، رقابت میان بازیگران بازار آنلاین طلا را عاملی برای توسعه خدمات جدید دانست. افزونی به دیجیاتو میگوید: «ما به عنوان یک کسبوکار از رقابت استقبال میکنیم. زمانی که رقابت شکل میگیرد، خودبهخود منجر به افزایش فیچرها و تعریف سرویسها و خدمات جدیدتر میشود.» به گفته او، بازار طلای آنلاین هنوز به سمت انحصار یک بازیگر حرکت نکرده و حضور چند بازیگر بزرگ در این حوزه، به تقسیم بازار میان آنها منجر شده است. افزونی معتقد است نتیجه چنین رقابتی در مرحله اول به نفع کاربران خواهد بود، زیرا کسبوکارها برای حفظ یا افزایش سهم خود، ناچار به توسعه خدمات و قابلیتهای جدید میشوند. حرکت از خریدوفروش ساده به ابزارهای متنوعتر صحبتهای افزونی نشان میدهد طلاین در مسیر توسعه محصول خود، به دنبال پاسخ به نیازهای متفاوت کاربران است؛ از کاربرانی که تجربه ساده خرید و فروش طلا را دنبال میکنند تا گروهی که به ابزارهای بیشتری برای تعیین زمان و قیمت معاملات خود نیاز دارند. بازار پیشرفته در این میان، یکی از نخستین گامهای طلاین برای ارائه چنین ابزارهایی است و این شرکت میگوید توسعه آن ادامه خواهد داشت. از سوی دیگر، تأکید افزونی بر رقابت نشان میدهد او توسعه قابلیتهای جدید را تنها به استراتژی داخلی یک پلتفرم محدود نمیداند. از نگاه او، حضور بازیگران متعدد و رقابت میان آنها میتواند کسبوکارها را به سمت توسعه خدمات متنوعتر سوق دهد؛ مسیری که در نهایت، کاربر نهایی گزینهها و ابزارهای بیشتری برای فعالیت در بازار آنلاین طلا خواهد داشت.
impact: ورود ابزارهای معامله‌گری حرفه‌ای به پلتفرم‌های آنلاین طلا، رقابت آن‌ها با بازار سنتی را وارد مرحله جدیدی می‌کند.

title_fa: تعطیلی پلتفرم ترابری TruckSmarter پس از جذب نیرو توسط خریدار
title_en: TruckSmarter Shutting Down
summary: اپلیکیشن TruckSmarter که نیم میلیون راننده کامیون از آن استفاده می‌کردند، به‌طور ناگهانی تعطیل شد.
این اتفاق نمونه‌ای شفاف از روند Acquihire است که در آن خریدار فقط تیم متخصص AI را جذب کرده و محصول را متوقف می‌کند.
صاحبان بار و رانندگان باید ظرف چند روز به پلتفرم‌های جایگزین نقل‌مکان کنند.
full_text: TruckSmarter announced on Tuesday that it has been acquired and that its driver app, Dispatch, shuts down on Friday, September 4. The scale is what makes this more than a routine startup wind-down. More than 500,000 carriers have used the TruckSmarter platform, which included a free load board alongside the paid Dispatch product. Dispatch was an AI chat interface that let a driver ask for freight in plain language and had software agents handle the bidding and booking, rather than making the driver work a traditional load board. Automated replies from the company indicated that active Dispatch subscriptions are canceled Friday, and that invoices paid within the previous 30 days will be refunded within seven business days of cancellation. Co-founder and chief executive Dan Kao posted a message inside the app thanking users for five years of trust, and drivers and trucking groups spread screenshots of it across social media. One thing has been ruled out. OTR Solutions, which bought TruckSmarter's factoring and banking division in November 2025, told FreightWaves it did not acquire the remaining business. So a company that raised money twelve months ago is gone by Friday, and nobody will say who bought it. That combination has a name in technology, even if no one involved here has used it. What an Acquihire Actually Is An acquihire is an acquisition where the buyer's real objective is the team rather than the business. The purchase price is justified by the engineers, product people and founders who come along with it, not by the revenue, the customers or the product they built. The word is a compression of acquisition and hire, and the mechanics are closer to hiring than to buying. A company that wants twenty experienced AI engineers can spend eighteen months recruiting them one at a time, competing against every other firm in the market, or it can buy the company those engineers already work at and get the whole team on day one, already functional, already used to working together. The second path is faster and often cheaper per head. What happens next is the part that matters to users. In a conventional acquisition, the buyer wants the product and keeps it running, because the customers are the asset. In an acquihire, the product is frequently shut down within weeks, because the product was never the point. Maintaining software the buyer does not want costs money, invites support obligations and distracts the team the buyer just paid for. Killing it is the rational move.
impact: سردرگمی شدید در بازار ترابری و نمایش خطرات تصاحب‌های تیمی استارتاپ‌ها برای کاربران نهایی.

title_fa: جنجال‌های ایمنی حول محور مدل جدید Astra از OpenAI
title_en: Researchers fear safety disaster ahead of OpenAI’s Astra release
summary: عرضه پرچمدار جدید OpenAI به دلیل حملات خودسرانه ایجنت‌ها در تست‌های ایمنی به تأخیر افتاد.
استفاده از معماری حلقوی باعث شده فرآیند تفکر مدل مخفی بماند و تحلیل رفتار آن برای محققان دشوار شود.
کارشناسان هشدار می‌دهند عدم شفافیت در استدلال مدل، خطرات امنیتی جبران‌ناپذیری به همراه دارد.
full_text: OpenAI is on the cusp of releasing its most powerful AI model yet, Astra, following weeks of delays to shore up safety protocols after its agents attacked real targets during testing. As details about the model trickle out, researchers are warning it “may be the single worst development for AI security/safety to date.” Researchers fear safety disaster ahead of OpenAI’s Astra release A report triggered concerns about a safety ‘race to the bottom.’ A report triggered concerns about a safety ‘race to the bottom.’ Shortly after OpenAI said on Tuesday that it had delayed Astra’s release to work on safety issues, The Information reported that Astra shows far less of its “thinking” than other frontier AI models, sparking concern it could be dangerously hard to monitor. Most top AI systems today are built using a technology known as a transformer, which processes some types of information linearly through layers before producing an answer. Models can be made to show their reasoning as they go, essentially “thinking out loud.” This “chain of thought” allows researchers and automated safety systems to monitor what AI models are doing and potentially spot undesirable behavior, such as lying or plans to circumvent safety guardrails, before they act. According to The Information, citing an unnamed person familiar with the unreleased model’s development, Astra uses a more opaque technique known as a recurrent depth or looped transformer, which cycles information through internal layers before producing an output. This would mean much more of the model’s “thinking” happens inside the system, and in a form that looks a lot less like natural human language, rather than being expressed in a way that researchers can easily monitor. This can boost model performance, but makes potential threats and unwanted behavior harder to detect. OpenAI has limited its use of the looped transformer / recurrent depth technique with Astra so researchers can continue to monitor the model’s reasoning, according to The Information’s unnamed source. In a blog post published Tuesday, OpenAI said it is “deploying Astra with additional chain-of-thought monitoring to rapidly detect and contain potentially misaligned actions.” It did not mention if the model has a different technical foundation. The Information’s report sparked widespread concern among AI safety researchers on social media. It was Redwood Research’s chief scientist Ryan Greenblatt, one of three outsiders OpenAI permitted to research the Hugging Face hack, who said a decision to use a more opaque architecture for Astra “may be the single worst development for AI security/safety to date.” Greenblatt said the investigation into the Hugging Face incident relied heavily on the models’ chain-of-thought, warning that less visible reasoning could allow AI systems to devise and execute strategies that would be far harder for researchers to detect. Greenblatt’s primary concern, echoed by other safety experts, is that competition to develop more advanced AI systems could lead to “a race to the bottom on architectures that could be catastrophic for our ability to oversee/monitor AIs” — with developers adopting increasingly opaque systems to gain an edge until models become difficult, or even impossible, to monitor. He added that OpenAI’s communications left him concerned that the company “plans on being extremely reliant on chain-of-thought monitoring for safety.” OpenAI bigwigs responded to the criticism in a series of social media posts that do not explicitly deny the company’s use of the technique. Several expressed concerns about the possibility of unmonitorable AI or a race to the bottom in terms of transparency, including OpenAI safety researchers Micah Carroll and Tomek Korbak, head of strategic futures Dean Ball, and chief scientist Jakub Pachocki, who voiced fears of “a race into unmonitorability kicked off by confused reporting.” He said the depth of Astra’s computation — a measure of how many steps it can perform internally — “is within a factor of two of GPT-4,” indicating that if the technique was used, the increased opacity is less dramatic than some reactions imply. OpenAI did not respond to The Verge’s request to confirm or deny whether looped transformers were used for Astra and directed us to Pachocki’s X post. “OpenAI has worked to preserve and utilize chain-of-thought monitoring since our very first reasoning models,” Pachocki wrote, adding that such monitoring “is fragile and unfortunately trending in a negative direction, for reasons not contingent on architecture changes that I will write about soon.” Most Popular - Sonos introduces new headphones, soundbar, and software in its biggest announcement in years - Dyson made a camera-equipped toothbrush that flosses for you - GoPro has been acquired and is getting into ‘defense, government, robotics and aerospace’ - Is this the future of America? - The rise of AI ‘civilizations’ and the fall of corporate responsibility
impact: احتمال کند شدن روند عرضه مدل‌های بعدی و فشار شدیدتر رگولاتورها بر استانداردهای ایمنی OpenAI.

title_fa: همکاری چندساله گوگل و مستربیست برای تبلیغ Gemini
title_en: Google is sending MrBeast into the wilderness, armed with AI
summary: مستربیست در ویدیوهای جدید خود از چت‌بات Gemini برای مسیریابی و بقا در شرایط سخت محیطی استفاده می‌کند.

full_text: MrBeast will feature Gemini, Google Health, and the Fitbit Air in upcoming videos as part of a multi-year partnership with Google. The deal will kick off with a video featuring Jimmy “MrBeast” Donaldson turning to Gemini for wilderness survival advice: Google is sending MrBeast into the wilderness, armed with AI One of YouTube’s biggest creators has a new deal to promote Gemini and Google Health. One of YouTube’s biggest creators has a new deal to promote Gemini and Google Health. First up on September 5 is a new MrBeast video following Jimmy and his crew as they attempt to survive some of the most extreme and treacherous climates on Earth. Teams will race to navigate three of the planet’s most unforgiving landscapes — the jungle, the desert, and the Arctic — using Gemini to help them identify dangers, survive brutal weather changes, and stay one step ahead. Google says Donaldson will also use a Fitbit Air in one of his upcoming challenges and appear in a Gemini campaign from Google. The deal comes a couple of months after Donaldson’s YouTube channel became the first to hit 500 million subscribers, and a recent Bloomberg report saying YouTube has been offering prominent creators deals to keep their content exclusive to its site as more creators strike deals with Netflix. title_fa: رونمایی از ترموستات Tado X برای پر کردن جای خالی Nest
title_en: Tado’s new thermostat is designed as a Nest killer
summary: شرکت تادو نسل دوم ترموستات Smart Thermostat X را با قیمت پایه ۱۶۰ پوند برای بازار اروپا معرفی کرد.
این گجت از پروتکل Matter-over-Thread پشتیبانی می‌کند و بدنه بسیار باریک‌تری نسبت به نسل قبل دارد.
تادو به‌طور مستقیم کاربران اروپایی گوگل Nest را هدف گرفته که پس از خروج گوگل بدون پشتیبانی مانده‌اند.
full_text: When Google ignominiously exited the European thermostat market last year, it pointed its customers to Tado. This week, the German-based smart home company is launching its Smart Thermostat X (2nd gen), and aiming to attract European Nest users who haven’t already jumped ship. Tado’s new thermostat is designed as a Nest killer But it’s for Europe, only. But it’s for Europe, only. Google shutting down the servers for its 1st- and 2nd-gen thermostats drove “significant sales” for Tado, Christian Deilmann, cofounder and managing director of Tado, told The Verge in an interview. The third-generation Nest has at least 10 times the penetration in Europe, he says. And while Google still supports it, Deilmann sees the writing on the wall. “At some point, I think they will continue their strategy,” he says. “There’s nothing we know for sure … but it doesn’t make too much sense to pull out of some generations and not others.” Tado’s newest thermostat costs £159.99/€179.99 for a wired starter kit and £169.99/€199.99 for a wireless kit. It has a completely new look, with a white square design and a circular interface that appears only when you touch it. At 17.8mm thick, it’s significantly slimmer than the first-gen Tado, and the third-gen Nest (Google never launched the fourth-gen in Europe). Deilmann says it’s designed to blend better into your home rather than stand out, as the previous all-black model did. There’s a customizable action button on the top, and the battery version lasts a year on its rechargeable battery. The Smart Thermostat X is designed to work with boilers, heat pumps, and underfloor heating (not air conditioning), and thanks to Matter-over-Thread connectivity, it can communicate more easily with a receiver sitting in a basement next to your boiler, as well as most smart home platforms. Tado moved to Thread from a proprietary 6LoWPAN with the first-gen Tado X. With the launch of the second-gen model, Tado is also rolling out new features across its line, including the ability to manage multiple thermostats in different homes under one account. Additionally, its hydronic balancing system, which works with its Smart Radiator Thermostat X to digitally balance radiators so the last one in the chain gets heat, is now TÜV certified, making it eligible for government heat-pump subsidies in certain markets. This feature requires Tado’s AI Assist, which costs £3.99 a month (£29.99 a year) and automatically optimizes heating based on weather conditions and your home’s characteristics. It includes options such as automatic geofencing, open-window detection, adaptive heating, and preheating before arrival. Tado is also launching a new energy savings promise. “We’re so confident about the benefit of our products and the value which we’re delivering in terms of energy cost savings — a few hundred euros every year for all of our customers,” says Deilmann. “If in the first 12 months you believe you haven’t saved enough energy or energy costs, then you can return all your products and get your money back, no questions asked.” The Smart Thermostat X (2nd gen) is available starting today from tado.com and at select European retailers. title_fa: ادوبی استارتاپ هوش مصنوعی Rilo را تصاحب کرد
title_en: Adobe acquires Indian market intelligence startup Rilo
summary: ادوبی برای تقویت سیستم‌های اتوماسیون مارکتینگ، استارتاپ هندی Rilo و تیم شش‌نفره آن را خریده است.
با انجام این معامله، خدمات Rilo کاملاً متوقف شده و فناوری آن به ابزارهای سازمانی ادوبی منتقل می‌شود.
این دومین تصاحب ادوبی در هند محسوب می‌شود و تمرکز این غول نرم‌افزاری بر خودکارسازی کمپین‌ها را پررنگ می‌کند.
full_text: Adobe has acquired India-based marketing intelligence startup Rilo in a deal involving licensing and team acquisition, TechCrunch learned and the company confirmed. This is Adobe’s second acquisition from India after it bought video platform Rephrase.ai in 2023. The companies didn’t disclose the deal’s terms. Beyond confirming the deal, Adobe declined to comment. The acquisition gives Adobe a small team and technology focused on automating marketing workflows, which have been changing as companies use AI to build tools to automate the creation, deployment, and tracking of campaigns, get action items from meetings or calls to complete tasks, and increase brand visibility on platforms like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. Rilo’s technology could bolster Adobe’s existing products as the company targets its larger customers. Founded by IIT batchmates Georgi Boby and Dhruv Jaglan in 2025, Rilo raised $1 million from investors including Peak XV, DeVC, and Day Zero Ventures at a $10 million valuation. A source told TechCrunch that investors will get an exit from this deal, and Adobe will integrate some of Rilo’s IP along with the six-member team. Jaglan mentioned on LinkedIn that more than 10,000 people had tried out the tool. The company worked on letting go-to-market teams create custom workflows, including competitor intelligence, content repurposing and distribution, and sales call analysis. It also allowed teams to set up custom workflows comparable to tools like Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work. Post-acquisition, Rilo will shut down and won’t be available to its customers. “We’re very excited that Rilo has been acquired by Adobe in such a short span of time,” Rahul Gupta, managing partner, Day Zero Ventures told TechCrunch over email. “Their workflow builder product was way ahead of the curve and shall be extremely valuable to a giant like Adobe in enhancing customer experience and productivity.” Adobe made a marquee marketing acquisition last year by buying SEO optimization company Semrush for $1.9 billion. DeVC’s Rahul Mathur told TechCrunch that Rilo could fit into Adobe’s CX and marketing suite to handle complex workflows and give customers visibility into actions they take on the creative company’s platform. Rivals like Canva have also bolstered their marketing portfolio with acquisitions and new launches. Meanwhile, Amazon, Google, and Meta have built their own AI-powered marketing rails. The story has been updated with co-founders’ post mentioning the stat.

title_fa: ادوبی ابزارهای هوش مصنوعی خود را به اسلک آورد
title_en: Adobe is making its tools available in Slack
summary: کاربران اسلک بدون خروج از برنامه، به فتوشاپ، فایرفلای و پریمیر دسترسی پیدا کردند.
ربات هوش مصنوعی اسلک با درک کانتکست چت‌ها، دستورات متنی را مستقیم به خروجی تصویری و ویدیویی تبدیل می‌کند.
ادوبی قصد دارد حضور خود را در تمامی چت‌بات‌های بزرگ بازار از جمله کلود و Gemini گسترش دهد.
full_text: Customers can now use Adobe’s apps like Firefly, Adobe Express, Photoshop, Premiere, Acrobat, InDesign, Illustrator, Stock, Lightroom, and others directly with Slack’s AI chatbot, Slackbot, Adobe announced on Monday. In addition, more than 70 Adobe tools will become available in Slack through the Adobe for Slack MCP app. With the Slackbot integration, users will be able to describe what they want to do, and the bot will call the right Adobe tool to complete the task. Adobe said that while calling its tools, Slackbot also takes in the context of the conversations. For instance, users can get information from conversations or Canvas and turn it into PDFs, images, and videos. They can also bring in assets from previous campaigns or the Creative Cloud asset library into a chat and edit them. At launch, this integration will be available to Slack Business+ and Enterprise+ teams. While productivity and creative companies have been busy adding AI features into their tools, most people still work in conversational boxes. This pushes the tool providers to make their features available through services like ChatGPT, Claude, and Slack. Last month, Adobe introduced a similar integration for ChatGPT and is planning to launch a Gemini integration soon. Deepti Pradeep, senior director for Agentic AI at Adobe, told TechCrunch over email that people are using the company’s tool in other apps for repeatable workflows like batch-editing images or resizing creatives without leaving the app. “In focus groups, people talked about the value they get from this experience very clearly: saving time, getting to the outcome they want faster without having to micromanage every step, being able to access Adobe wherever they’re already working. That’s been interesting for us because it’s pushed us to think less about individual edits and more about the larger outcome someone is trying to get to,” Pradeep said. Other creative tools like Canva and Figma are also making their capabilities available in chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude. On the other hand, companies like Anthropic are releasing tighter integrations in Slack, because team context is often captured through those conversations. Pradeep said that consumers having choices between tools is a good thing, but Adobe has the advantage of providing both creative and productive tools across different modalities.
impact: حذف نیاز به سوئیچ بین ابزارها و افزایش سرعت گردش‌کار تیم‌های خلاق در محیط چت.
